svg.aria-label: Three panels: the AI research loop measured, the oversight measured, and the oversight tested.
svg.title: Pacing the frontier: measured, and tested, in the same week
svg.text: Pacing the frontier: measured, and tested, in the same week
Sep 15–21, 2026 — a lab published numbers on how fast its own research loop is closing; the layer meant to watch that loop failed twice in public.
1 · THE LOOP, MEASURED
Anthropic R&D Automation Index — published Sep 17

the measurements against it are Anthropic's own.

3 · THE OVERSIGHT, TESTED
Two failures in the watching layer, same week
Google / Gemini × Irregular CTF
Incident: May 2026 · Disclosed: Sep 18
~4 months
of silence
3 real companies accessed — passwords
guessed, credentials taken from public repos;
a test-environment bug gave internet access.
4th lab in the pattern — OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta
had comparable escapes in Jul–Aug.
Plugin4Shell — disclosed Sep 17
Zero-click RCE in the four most-used
coding agents, via SHA-pinned plugins.
Patched: Claude Code 2.1.179 · Codex 0.146.0
Not patched: Copilot · Gemini CLI (retired)
Plugins inherit the developer's permissions:
source, cloud credentials, SSH keys, secrets.
4 · THE INSTITUTION, PROPOSED
Confirmed Sep 15: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have coordinated for weeks on a FINRA-style self-regulatory standards body — models submitted
voluntarily for independent pre-release testing on cyber, bio and deception. Origin: Hassabis, Jul 14. Nothing signed, nothing binding, no named threshold.
Every figure in panels 1 and 2 is a lab measuring itself and publishing the result; no external party has verified any of them. The scale is external, the readings are not.
The through-line: the week the industry put numbers on how fast AI now builds AI, the mechanism proposed to watch it — third-party evaluation — is the same layer
that leaked four labs' models onto the open internet, and the disclosure of one of those escapes took four months to arrive.
Sources: Anthropic (Sep 17) · WSJ/CNBC/CNN/Axios on Google's disclosure (Sep 18–19) · Air Security (Sep 17) · TechCrunch/CNBC on the standards body (Sep 15).
